description: TERRAFORM (Planetary Analog Intelligence) is a geospatial research project that uses satellite imagery, Earth observation data, and planetary datasets to identify and compare Earth environments with the geological and environmental conditions of the Moon and Mars. It aims to develop an interactive platform supporting planetary research, scientific visualization, and future space exploration.

TERRAFORM — Planetary Analog Intelligenc

TERRAFORM is a geospatial research platform developed to identify and investigate terrestrial environments that exhibit measurable terrain similarities to planetary landscapes on Mars and the Moon. It brings together planetary elevation datasets and Earth observation data to perform comparative terrain analysis through metrics such as elevation, slope, surface roughness, and local relief.

The platform processes geospatial datasets, compares terrain characteristics across planetary bodies, identifies preliminary candidate regions, and presents findings through interactive maps, statistical visualizations, and regional research reports. Demonstrations include comparisons between Chile's Atacama Desert and Mars' Jezero Crater, alongside broader Mars and Moon terrain investigations.

By making planetary terrain comparisons more accessible, transparent, and reproducible, TERRAFORM provides a foundation for exploring potential terrestrial analog environments. Such investigations can support planetary science, mission site research, field studies, and a better understanding of Earth's value as a reference for future exploration of other worlds.
details:
Project Details — TERRAFORM: Planetary Analog Intelligence

TERRAFORM is an interactive geospatial research platform designed to investigate similarities between terrestrial landscapes on Earth and planetary terrain on Mars and the Moon. Its primary objective is to identify preliminary Earth-based analogue environments that can help researchers understand, study, and simulate extraterrestrial landscapes.

How It Works

TERRAFORM follows a data-driven geospatial analysis pipeline. It integrates Earth observation and planetary elevation datasets, processes terrain information, and extracts measurable characteristics for comparative investigation.

The platform's workflow consists of:

  1. Data Integration: Organizing and processing available Earth, Mars, and Moon geospatial datasets.
  2. Terrain Characterization: Calculating and examining terrain properties, including elevation, slope, surface roughness, and local relief.
  3. Statistical Comparison: Comparing terrain characteristics across different planetary environments using quantitative analysis.
  4. Candidate Identification: Extracting geographically connected regions that exhibit potentially comparable terrain characteristics.
  5. Geospatial Visualization: Presenting research findings through interactive maps, statistical graphs, comparison outputs, and regional reports.

The platform includes investigations such as comparing Chile's Atacama Desert with Mars' Jezero Crater, alongside broader planetary terrain comparisons and regional studies involving Death Valley.

Benefits and Intended Impact

TERRAFORM aims to make planetary analogue investigation more accessible through an integrated and reproducible geospatial workflow. Earth-based analogue environments can provide valuable reference locations for studying extraterrestrial terrain, supporting field research, scientific experimentation, equipment testing, and the preparation of future planetary exploration activities.

By identifying potential similarities through measurable terrain characteristics rather than visual resemblance alone, the platform provides a more structured approach to preliminary analogue screening. Its outputs are intended to support further scientific investigation, not replace geological field validation or mission-site qualification.

Technologies and Development Tools

The project was developed primarily using Python and its scientific and geospatial ecosystem:

  • Python: Core programming language and analytical engine.
  • NumPy: Numerical computation and array-based processing.
  • Pandas: Dataset management and statistical data handling.
  • Rasterio: Geospatial raster processing.
  • GeoPandas: Geospatial vector data analysis.
  • Folium: Interactive geographical mapping.
  • Plotly: Interactive statistical visualizations.
  • Streamlit: Interactive research dashboard and user interface.
  • CSV, JSON, GeoTIFF and XLSX: Data storage, processing, and research outputs.
  • Visual Studio Code: Development environment.
  • Git and GitHub: Version control and project hosting.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of TERRAFORM lies in bringing planetary science, Earth observation, statistical analysis, and interactive geospatial intelligence into one research platform. Instead of treating planetary analogue identification as a purely visual exercise, TERRAFORM investigates measurable terrain characteristics and uses comparative analysis to screen potential terrestrial environments.

The platform is also designed around modularity, allowing additional geographical regions, planetary datasets, and analytical capabilities to be incorporated as the research develops.

Factors Considered

During development, we considered dataset availability, spatial resolution, geographical coverage, terrain variability, comparability of measurements, processing requirements, and the limitations of available elevation data. We also considered the importance of distinguishing preliminary terrain similarities from scientifically verified geological analogues.

Ultimately, TERRAFORM is intended to serve as an expandable foundation for planetary analogue research, helping connect the landscapes of Earth with the challenges of exploring other worlds.
